decision.summary: Single chirp every minute from a sealed CO alarm fitted 2019 with 7-year life, so most likely end-of-life, not an active CO emergency or a battery issue. Logged urgent JOB-101 and routine fan JOB-102, gave the tenant safety advice, and asked the landlord to approve replacement.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery or end-of-life alarm? How decided?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life: the alarm is a sealed unit fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year life (expired about April 2026), and the signal is an intermittent chirp rather than a continuous alarm. Not a user-replaceable battery. Not treated as a confirmed CO emergency, but a real leak is not ruled out, so safety advice was given and it is urgent.

answers.question: Who is responsible, citing clause?
answers.answer: Landlord. Clause 12.8 only makes the tenant replace batteries; this is a sealed alarm past its life so it needs replacing as equipment. Clause 12.9 requires the tenant to report faults, which she did. Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out charge) does not apply as the call-out is not avoidable.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (urgent) and JOB-102 (routine fan), texted Priya (no battery removal, ventilate, symptoms/continuous alarm means leave and call 999 and 0800 111 999, 72h target, landlord's responsibility), requested landlord approval within £300 limit, scheduled follow-up 2026-10-11.

args.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Your CO alarm is a sealed unit fitted in 2019 and is past its 7-year life, so the chirp is most likely it reaching end of life. Please don't take the battery out or cover it (it's sealed anyway), and don't assume it's harmless. Open a window for fresh air. If anyone has a headache, dizziness, nausea or feels drowsy, or the alarm goes into a continuous loud alarm, leave the flat, call 999, and call the Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999. We've logged this as urgent (JOB-101) and are arranging a replacement alarm and a check, target within 72 hours; we'll update you. Replacing a sealed alarm is the landlord's job, not yours. We've also logged the noisy bathroom fan separately (JOB-102) as routine.
